lines.text: The cut blocks stop short. Black water lies between the last one and the far passage, and the cold comes up off it like breath.
It’s most of the way to ice already. It only wants telling.
That’ll bear. It’ll keep, too. Nothing down here is in a hurry to thaw.
The end of the seam. The cutters followed the best of the granite this far, and took it out whole.
A row of hollows in the face, each the size of a block. Three lines are cut across each other over every one, and there is a name under every one, worn down to scratches.
The last hollow is the cleanest. Its name panel has been dressed smooth, ready for the chisel. Nothing is cut in it.
Taken out whole. Every one. That's not quarrying. That's fetching.
Panel's dressed and nobody's lettered it. Somebody paid for that and never came back.
